new_statements.quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) Stress is phonemic: 'ifo 'knee' i'bo 'nose' [...] Conventions: Orthographic Phonemic stress is not written.
new_statements.citation: Weimer, Harry. 1992. Organised Phonology Data: Aneme Wake (Abia, Upper Musa) language [ABY], Oro Province. Ukarumpa, PNG: Summer Institute of Linguistics. 4 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 42353, 'Aneme Wake Organised Phonology Paper'; data checked by Harry Weimer, May 1992.)
new_statements.locator: p. 3, sections 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' and 'Conventions: Orthographic'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (4 pp., born-digital text layer; also rendered p.3 at 150 dpi and read the page image). At p.3 under the bold heading 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)' the sheet reads exactly: "Stress is phonemic: 'ifo 'knee' i'bo 'nose'"; under 'Conventions: Orthographic': "Phonemic stress is not written." Both quoted lines are verbatim (the first reader's [...] elides the Syllable Patterns table and the 'Conventions: Phonological' paragraph). Nothing else in the OPD bears on stress: no default position, no weight statement, no secondary stress. Reading: a bare 'stress is phonemic' with a disyllabic near-minimal pair (initial 'ifo vs second-syllable i'bo) and no positional rule = lexi…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is contrastive (lexically specified), demonstrated by the near-minimal pair 'ifo 'knee' (initial stress) vs i'bo 'nose' (second-syllable stress); no positional default is stated. The OPD's syllable-pattern examples (stressed syllable in bold) show stress on initial (o.ma 'stone', bo.ra, wai.ro), medial (ka.e.ma 'sweet potato', me.ra.ma 'bad') and final syllables (a.ma.e 'mother', u.si 'stick', bo.kai 'head', su.bu.ai 'cassowary'). Stress is not marked in the orthography.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the sheet gives only the contrast and examples. (For the sister language Yareba, Weimer & Weimer 1972 restrict contrastive stress to the first or second syllable of stems; no such restriction is stated for Aneme Wake, and the OPD examples include final stress on trisyllables.)
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, citation forms in a 4-page SIL-PNG Organised Phonology Data sheet; no acoustic or phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD is explicitly for 'Aneme Wake (Abia, Upper Musa) [ABY]', villages Dari (Jari) and Safia, Oro Province = Glottolog anem1248 / ISO aby. Weimer 1977 notes Dutton subsumed Aneme Wake under his 'Abia' language and that the Weimers had no data from 'Abie/Abia' proper at that time; the 1992 OPD treats Abia as an alternate name of Aneme Wake. The 1977/1978 family manuscripts are filed in the SIL archive under Yareba [yrb] but include Aneme Wake columns.
